patches.entity_key: Use of subjunctive after verbs of wish and desire
value: The subjunctive verb agrees with its own subject, which differs from the main clause subject (Je veux que tu achètes).
When the subjects are the same, the infinitive replaces the clause and carries no person agreement.

evidence.notes: Two-subject construction: each verb agrees with its own subject; same-subject construction uses an invariable infinitive. AI-generated, unverified.

value: on always takes third-person singular verb agreement, whatever its meaning (on va, on parle).
When on informally replaces nous, the verb still stays third-person singular.

evidence.notes: On is a third-person singular subject pronoun in all its uses. AI-generated, unverified.

patches.entity_key: Using -ci and -là to distinguish between two elements
value: -ci and -là are invariable particles; they do not agree with the noun.
The demonstrative adjective, not the particle, marks the noun's gender and number (ce livre-ci, cette maison-là).

evidence.notes: Particles attach to the noun but carry no gender/number features themselves. AI-generated, unverified.

value: on takes third-person singular verb agreement (On parle anglais ici).
The verb agrees with on, not with the logical object of the action.

evidence.notes: Impersonal on is grammatically third-person singular regardless of the semantic object. AI-generated, unverified.

value: Verb agrees with the subject in person and number (je viens, nous venons, ils reviennent).
Derivatives such as devenir, prévenir, revenir, and survenir keep the same agreement pattern as venir.

evidence.notes: Derivative verbs share venir's irregular stem but retain full subject agreement. AI-generated, unverified.

patches.entity_key: Verbs followed by preposition de before infinitive
value: The main verb agrees with its subject in person and number; the infinitive carries no agreement.
The preposition de is invariable and introduces the dependent infinitive.

evidence.notes: Prepositional infinitive complements leave agreement on the conjugated verb only. AI-generated, unverified.

patches.entity_key: Verbs followed by preposition à before infinitive
value: The main verb agrees with its subject in person and number; the infinitive carries no agreement.
The preposition à is invariable before an infinitive and does not contract with an article.

evidence.notes: à + infinitive is a fixed prepositional pattern; agreement remains on the conjugated verb. AI-generated, unverified.

value: The conjugated verb agrees with its subject in person and number; the infinitive carries no agreement.
When the subjects differ, a que clause is used and its verb agrees with its own subject.

evidence.notes: Direct infinitive construction requires the same subject; a subject change forces a que clause with its own agreement. AI-generated, unverified.

value: The impersonal il is always third-person singular, so faire stays in the il fait form.
There is no agreement with a real subject, since impersonal il has no referent.

evidence.notes: il fait beau, il fait froid: fixed impersonal third-person singular. AI-generated, unverified.

value: The conditional form of vouloir agrees with the subject in person and number (je voudrais, voudriez-vous).
The infinitive following vouloir carries no agreement.

evidence.notes: Politeness uses the conditional, whose endings still mark person and number. AI-generated, unverified.
